--- Page 1 (Beckerman_14a) --- Dear Jack, With today a holiday and 2 of your letters waiting to be answered there's no reason for not making that the business of the moment. He found the enclosures very interesting and will worth the 6 additional postage that was due. I've waiting for the pictures to come out from the developing process but the two we did glimpse were swell shots. The office newspapers were equally interesting even though the names were not familiar. But that crack about remembrance of Tree Gaws in Brooklyn when it was a flatbush didn't need any personal introductions to be appreciated as a juicy bit of corn... 'York' magazine has just arrived too and will be thoroughly reviewed by all hands. Thanks for all the literature; it's being read to good advantage. About the records - we will definitely read some as soon as we consult Leah on the specific numbers and we shouldn't have any trouble getting by the P.O. clerk with those bona fide requests. He really were surprised, tho' very glad to hear that there's some chance of your getting to see. At first we had thought of it only in the realm of wishful thinking. But that it's turned out to be more of an... [illegible] to that vicinity, we're once again [illegible] for those pictures of you [illegible] together. : ) Today is Washington's 213 birthday but we also associate the day with the end of your 3rd year of army life and the beginning of Abe's 2nd year overseas; so it has both national and domestic significance, but the sooner we cut out the... [illegible] season too, [illegible] --- Page 2 (Beckerman_14b) --- Papa has been working steadily of late, and is feeling all right also. The news behind the news of the steady season is that only 6 of the original 30 workers have remained faithful to the establishment. The rest are making their fortunes elsewhere. Mama has just finished writing a letter to Abe. What prompted it was a large, very lifelike picture we just received from him showing "X-mas in the Philippines" with a decorated tree & a group of boys (incl. Abe) standing around it waiting to shake the Chaplain's hand. What makes it so valiant is that Abe is standing in his habitual position, hands in pockets, feet turned out, & every wrinkle in his shirt seems alive. Nothing much else to make writing news except that about the starting of a new school term. With a program of Fr. Trg, Hist, Eng, P.S. Art & Sociology + a seminar in related soc. subjects + actual group work with a welfare org. it makes for a rather full week. The latter are extra cur. in line with majoring in Social Work. Luckily my program fitted very compactly into the first 4 hours of each day; that is it did after 2 classes were conveniently spent. The teacher in charge was very nice about it. Since this is the first term that girls have made their appearance upstairs in any notice/numbers he didn't have the heart to see any of them disappointed in any way. He also got a breath of air between classes now, tramping from on his own. There is + is a 20 min. train ride. It's much to early to begin worrying about marks and the like, but you really have to work for a living down here. No easy going Sanderson for Nist, nor will this last term of French leave any happy memories. Well there's always the campus! --- Page 3 (Beckerman_14c) --- All news certainly makes very good reading these days. Now the situation has been reversed in the past few weeks! The Red Army seems to be making that Victory into a closer reality each day. In the past 3 days the headlines have read: 200 mi to Berlin, 165, now it's 131! That's a magnificent pace and praise is forthcoming for every pound! It's icy cold out right now and the cold blasts make us wish we could give and take a little of the Australian temperature... Not much more news from here except concerning those little postal cards that are coming each day, and even that doesn't make for too good news. Expect in 26 things you can look forward to. The only the results of 3 out of 5 and they certainly make for variety as far as letters go. Starting with the best part they read A - Host B - French & C - Mark. That leaves Eva, G, & [illegible] --- Page 4 (Beckerman_14d) --- still on the waiting line but live a knowing feeling that they're not going to be what I'd like them to be. Well, next term starts a new leaf, and along with it go resolutions to come through with better gains. Well, we will cut this short now as a letter to Abe has to be written now too. He will be looking forward to more mail from you. By the way all your letters will come re-censored. - All are fine here and send Love. Regards Mama Papa Ruth
